H1 2026 cumulative: revenue KRW 114,761M (-42.5% YoY vs KRW 199,639M), operating LOSS KRW 5,608M (vs OP KRW 40,483M in H1 2025), net income KRW 4,310M (vs KRW 32,756M). H1 mix: semiconductor equipment KRW 112,574M (98.1%), display KRW 2,187M (1.9%), solar KRW 0; products KRW 88,918M (77.5%) / merchandise (parts and raw materials) KRW 25,843M (22.5%). quarterly_data.signal: ORDER BACKLOG (separate basis, excluding parts) at 2026-06-30: KRW 233,635M, up 3.1x from KRW 74.7B at Q1-end 2026 -- semiconductor equipment KRW 214,358M (orders received KRW 301,891M less KRW 87,533M delivered) and display equipment KRW 19,277M (nothing delivered yet); solar nil. Customers, delivery dates and unit counts are withheld (reported to the auditor as competitively sensitive). Contract liabilities (customer prepayments) fell to KRW 10,822M from KRW 41,831M at 2025-12-31 as KRW 32,074M of opening prepayments was recognised as revenue; contract assets rose to KRW 13,152M (gross KRW 32,349M less KRW 19,196M allowance). Revenue is recognised on delivery, not percentage-of-completion; semiconductor tool lead time 3-9 months, solar/display 10-12 months; domestic terms 90% on delivery / 10% on acceptance. Filing lists the prior disclosed SK Hynix supply contracts (2021-2022: KRW 13.0B, 14.5B, 12.1B, 14.5B, 32.9B, 15.2B, 30.3B; July 2024: KRW 19.4B) and the 2022-02 LG Display display-equipment contract (KRW 40.9B). Management committee minutes show repeated 'pre-emptive build of semiconductor equipment for domestic customers' resolutions (2026-01-29, 2026-03-26 retrofit, 2026-04-22) plus one 'additional budget for overseas semiconductor equipment build' (2026-05-21) and overseas display equipment build (2026-06-11).

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and capex (H1 2026): modular production capacity unchanged at 1,705 systems/year (semiconductor 1,617, display 88) at the Gwangju (Gyeonggi) plant; H1 output only 6 tools (5 semiconductor, 1 display) vs 18 in FY2025 and 43 in FY2024, yet reported UTILISATION 98.06% (22,153.9 of 22,592.0 available hours, outsourced staff included) because output excludes retrofits and relocations. Solar-cell equipment capacity stated as over 20 GWp/year, flexible with semiconductor/display schedules. Capex programme: Yongin R&D Center No. 2 (announced 2025-06-09), KRW 104.8B (18.5% of equity), 2025-06-09 to 2028-06-09, to add R&D fab space for semiconductor/display/solar synergy -- 'in progress'; H1 construction-in-progress additions KRW 3,857M, machinery transfers from inventory KRW 14,078M (demo/eval tools capitalised), depreciation KRW 10,164M. Land purchase agreement in the Yongin semiconductor cluster general industrial complex: KRW 15,740M total, KRW 14,166M already paid, final acquisition by December 2027. Raw-material purchases H1 KRW 92,222M: machined parts (aluminium etc.) KRW 31,175M (33.8%), OEM equipment KRW 21,681M (23.5%), OEM parts KRW 15,260M (16.5%), electrical/control components KRW 12,405M (13.5%), remote-plasma RF units KRW 1,535M, aluminium stock KRW 1,380M; no supplier named. Inventory KRW 46,037M (WIP KRW 29,967M net of KRW 15,337M write-down; H1 write-down expense KRW 4,804M). Sales subsidiaries: Jusung Inc. (US, Delaware, set up 2024), Jusung Europe GmbH, Jusung Taiwan, Jusung Shanghai (China revenue KRW 2,768M H1).

quarterly_data.signal: Products and catalysts: positioned as the world No. 4 ALD equipment vendor in 2025 (after ASM International, TEL, Lam Research; Gartner/Business Research Company: ALD market USD 3.93B in 2026, ~8% CAGR to USD 5.39B by 2030), specialised in High-k ALD for DRAM capacitors; the SDP (Space Divided Plasma) ALD/CVD platform is the main revenue engine and demand for High-k capability is expected to keep rising as capacitor scaling hits structural limits. NEW: Jusung says it recently SHIPPED an ALG (Atomic Layer Growth) TRANSISTOR FULL-INTEGRATION TOOL TO A GLOBAL CUSTOMER, opening a new market; ALG-based III-V / II-VI compound-semiconductor channel deposition below 400C on any substrate (electron mobility up to 8,500 cm2/Vs vs 1,400 for silicon) is being pushed into semiconductor mass-production lines and extended to display (glass-substrate inorganic micro-LED) and solar (tandem HJT+perovskite, 35%+ efficiency, also pitched for space AI data-center solar). Filing cites Korea's HBM-led advanced-memory capex as the 2026 driver (SEMI: global equipment USD 133B 2025 -> USD 165.9B 2026 (+23.2%) -> USD 229.5B 2028). Equipment lines: SD System (ALD/HDPCVD/Dry Etch/MOCVD/UHVCVD), ALMO/ALMO+, SDP, Guidance Series (ALG/ALD/CVD), Eureka Epi; display Oxide-TFT CVD ~40% global share, large-size Encapsulation 100%. Corporate: 787,200 treasury shares cancelled 2026-02-25 (KRW 40,856M; shares outstanding 46,481,121); credit rating cut to BBB+ by NICE D&B (2026-04-20) and eCredible (2026-04-22) from A-; new inside director Yoo Jin-hyuk (sales head) and independent director Kim Hyun-myung elected 2026-03-26; Park Kwon-sik (ex-LG Display research head) hired as Display/Solar division president; strategic stakes: Rebellions KRW 20,000M (1.15%), Syntiant KRW 3,000M (bought 2026-03-10), SanDisk KRW 12,250M and Intel KRW 3,960M (both bought 2026-06-24). Share price ran from KRW 33,431 average in January 2026 to KRW 202,124 average in June 2026 (high KRW 250,500); H1 TSR 625.6%. Dividend policy 5-20% payout; FY2025 dividend KRW 53/share.
